newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends up on central bank comments.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends up on central bank comments.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar ended slightly higher against the U.S. dollar on Thursday, rebounding after the central bank urged the market not to have "false expectations" of a depreciation following Wednesday's sharp downturn.
The local unit ended at T$27.559 to the U.S. dollar compared to Wednesday's T$27.586 close. Turnover through dealers was an active US$246.5 million.

Central bank vice-governor Liang Cheng-chin said late on Wednesday that Wednesday's sharp depreciation "was the result of market expectations" and added: "I hope the market will not have this sort of false expectations."
Dealers noted active profit-taking on U.S. dollars by foreign banks throughout the session.

"Foreign banks, which held a lot U.S. dollars in the Taiwan dollar depreciation, took profits after the central bank comments," said one dealer. "Some local banks also sold U.S. dollars for exporters," she said.
Dealers said the depreciation likely had come to an end but that further Taiwan dollar erosion could not be ruled out.
"As foreign equity funds have slowed their entries, giving less pressure for an appreciation, the Taiwan dollar should still be in a slight downtrend," another dealer said.
A T$27.52-60 trading range was seen for next week.
The market is closed on Friday and Saturday for a domestic holiday.
